faqs.question: What is a good quote for October?
faqs.answer: For a card, Thoreau's "October is the month for painted leaves" from "Autumnal Tints" (1862) is short, public domain and checkable on Project Gutenberg. For a caption, a line of under six words such as "Crisp air, clear head" fits one phone screen.

faqs.question: What did Thoreau say about October?
faqs.answer: In "Autumnal Tints" (1862) Thoreau wrote: "October is the month for painted leaves. Their rich glow now flashes round the world." The Gutenberg edition of Excursions reads "for", although many quote lists print "of".

faqs.question: Who wrote "Season of mists and mellow fruitfulness"?
faqs.answer: John Keats, as the first line of "To Autumn". He wrote it on 19 September 1819 and it was printed in his 1820 collection with Lamia and The Eve of St. Agnes.

faqs.question: What is a short "hello October" caption?
faqs.answer: Try "Hello October. Last quarter, first scarf." or "1 October: the day the candles come back out." Both are original to this page, so you can post them without credit.

faqs.question: Is Robert Frost's poem "October" public domain?
faqs.answer: In the US, yes: it was published in A Boy's Will in 1913. Frost died in 1963, so in life-plus-70 countries such as the UK it stays in copyright until the end of 2033; quoting a couple of lines with credit is fine, printing the whole poem on products is not.

faqs.question: Why do leaves change colour in October?
faqs.answer: Shorter days and cooler nights make leaves stop producing food, so the green chlorophyll breaks down. That reveals yellow and orange carotenes and xanthophylls that were there all summer, while red anthocyanins form fresh in autumn, according to SUNY ESF.

faqs.question: Does autumn really make people sad?
faqs.answer: Less than people assume. A 2020 PLOS ONE study of 5,282 Dutch adults found mood was slightly better in spring than in autumn, but the effects were small or very small and appeared only in people higher in neuroticism.

faqs.question: Can I use these October quotes on Instagram or in a shop?
faqs.answer: The original lines on this page can be used anywhere without credit. The Keats, Thoreau and Jackson lines are public domain everywhere; for products sold in the UK or EU, avoid printing Frost's poem.

faqs.question: How many days are in October, and when does it end?
faqs.answer: October has 31 days and is the 10th month of the year. It ends on 31 October, Halloween, followed by All Saints' Day on 1 November.

faqs.question: What should I write in an October card?
faqs.answer: Pair one classic line, such as Jackson's "The month of carnival of all the year", with a sentence of your own about a shared autumn memory. Keep it under 40 words so it reads well on a card or a phone.

faqs.question: What is a good October quote for a planner or letter board?
faqs.answer: Motivational lines of 4 to 12 words work best, such as "Shorter days, sharper focus" or "You do not need January to start again. October will do." On 1 October there are 92 days left in the year, which makes a useful planner prompt.

# October Quotes for the Whole Month, From Keats to Captions

The best October quotes cover the whole month, not only Halloween: checked autumn verse for a card, "hello October" lines for the 1st, and short captions for the leaves in between. Below are 6 public-domain lines matched word for word against Project Gutenberg, including Thoreau's 1862 "October is the month for painted leaves" (many lists print "of"), plus 55 original lines sorted by use. Keep them short: across SubhSandesh, 48.3% of shared pages are opened on a phone (27,725 of 57,456 views), and the average page is viewed 11.1 times, so the line you pick gets read on a small screen, more than once.

Below the lines sit the science of why leaves turn red and what a 5,282-person study found about autumn mood. A table then matches each theme to a caption, card or planner.

## 6 public-domain October and autumn lines, checked against Gutenberg

Each line below matches the Project Gutenberg text linked, spelling and punctuation included. October, the 10th month, has 31 days.

1. > "Season of mists and mellow fruitfulness, / Close bosom-friend of the maturing sun;"

   John Keats, "To Autumn", written 19 September 1819 and printed in [Keats: Poems Published in 1820](https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/23684). Keats was born on 31 October 1795.
2. > "Where are the songs of Spring? Ay, where are they? / Think not of them, thou hast thy music too,—"

   Keats, the third stanza of the same poem.
3. > "October is the month for painted leaves. Their rich glow now flashes round the world."

   Henry David Thoreau, "Autumnal Tints" (1862), in [Excursions](https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/9846) (1863). The Gutenberg text reads "for", not "of".
4. > "October is its sunset sky; November the later twilight."

   Thoreau, the same essay, three sentences later.
5. > "The month of carnival of all the year, / When Nature lets the wild earth go its way / And spend whole seasons on a single day."

   Helen Hunt Jackson, "October", in [A Calendar of Sonnets](https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/9825) (1886), published the year after her death.
6. > "O hushed October morning mild, / Thy leaves have ripened to the fall;"

   Robert Frost, "October", in [A Boy's Will](https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/3021) (London, 1913).

Emily Brontë's "Fall, leaves, fall" and Jackson's "October's Bright Blue Weather" are left out: no Gutenberg edition we found prints them to check against. One caution on Frost: he died in 1963, so "October" is public domain in the US but stays in copyright until the end of 2033 in countries with a life-plus-70 term, such as the UK.

## 55 original October quotes, sorted by use

Written for this page and kept clean. Use them anywhere; no credit needed.

### "Hello October" quotes for 1 October (8)

- Hello October. Thirty-one days, and I plan to notice every one.
- Hello October, bring the cold mornings and the warm kitchens.
- October is here, and the year has finally put the kettle on.
- New month, new light, same promise to slow down.
- Hello October. Last quarter, first scarf.
- Dear October, please be gentle with my to-do list.
- The tenth month is open. Wipe your boots and come in.
- 1 October: the day the candles come back out.

### Cosy and sweater-weather October quotes (9)

- Socks thick, tea strong, plans cancelled. October approves.
- My favourite forecast: high chance of blankets.
- October evenings are made for soup and long phone calls.
- Sleeves past my hands is my whole personality now.
- Rain on the window, a book on my lap, nowhere to be.
- The best night of October is the first one that needs a quilt.
- Cold hands, warm mug, slow Sunday.
- Lamps on at five, and nobody complaining.
- October asks for one thing: stay in a little longer.

### Leaves and harvest October quotes (9)

- The maples are spending all their gold at once.
- Every tree on my street is showing off, and I'm here for it.
- Apples in the bowl, leaves on the step, nothing out of place.
- October paints the hills and leaves the brushes on the path.
- The fields are cut, the barns are full, the evenings are ours.
- Crunch underfoot is October's way of saying keep walking.
- A red leaf pressed in a book is the smallest souvenir of the year.
- Harvest moon up, porch light on, cider warming.
- Somewhere a squirrel is better prepared for winter than me.

### Halloween countdown quotes for the last week of October (9)

- One week to Halloween and the costume is still a theory.
- Pumpkins bought, carving date pending.
- Thirty nights of cosy, one night of spooky.
- The countdown is on: fog machine charged, sweets hidden from myself.
- Every October night is a rehearsal for the 31st.
- Halloween is close enough to smell the candle wax.
- Three days left. The cat has already chosen her costume: cat.
- October saves its loudest party for its last night.
- Countdown status: webs up, nerves steady, chocolate stock dropping.

### Motivational "new season" October quotes (9)

- 92 days left on 1 October. Plenty of time to begin.
- Change is just the season doing its job. Do yours.
- October proves that endings can be the brightest part.
- Start the thing before the clocks change.
- Shorter days, sharper focus.
- New season, same goals, better coat.
- You do not need January to start again. October will do.
- Gather what you grew this year. Count it before you judge it.
- Be like October: honest about change, generous with colour.

### Short October captions, under six words (11)

- Oh my gourd, October.
- Leaf me alone, I'm cosy.
- Golden light, all month.
- Crisp air, clear head.
- Mug season.
- Officially in my scarf era.
- Ten out of ten month.
- Fog, fire, friends.
- Pumpkin o'clock.
- Orange you glad it's October?
- Peak cardigan month.

## Why October leaves turn red, orange and yellow

Leaves change colour because the green pigment breaks down and reveals, or adds, other pigments. [SUNY ESF's forestry explainer, "Why Leaves Change Color"](https://www.esf.edu/ecenter/eis/leaves.php), says that shorter daylight and falling temperatures make leaves stop making food, so chlorophyll breaks down and the green disappears.

The yellows and oranges were there all summer: carotenes and xanthophylls, the pigments that colour a carrot, masked by chlorophyll. The reds and purples are new, from anthocyanin pigments that form in autumn; ESF credits them for the reds of dogwoods and sumacs and, mixed with other pigments, the sugar maple's brilliant orange. Oaks lean brown.

Meanwhile a layer of cells cuts the leaf loose at the stalk and seals the wound. So Thoreau's "painted" leaves are partly unmasked rather than painted, worth a caption: "October doesn't add the gold. It just stops hiding it."

## Does October actually change your mood?

Less than most quote pages assume. Winthorst and colleagues surveyed 5,282 Dutch adults online and reported in [PLOS ONE in 2020](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC7489524) that people scored higher on positive affect and lower on depressive symptoms in spring than in summer, autumn or winter, and lower on negative affect in spring than in autumn.

The effects were "small or very small". Only participants higher in neuroticism showed seasonality at all, and the 503 who answered twice in different seasons showed no within-person change. Its autumn ran 21 September to 20 December.

So a cheerful "hello October" line is not fighting a universal autumn slump. For someone who struggles as the days shorten, a quote is a kindness, not care.

## Which October quote fits a caption, card or planner?

Lengths are the word range of this page's own examples. Pick by where the line will sit.

| Theme | Best use | Length | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| Public-domain verse | Card, letter, framed print | 9–25 words | "October is its sunset sky; November the later twilight." |
| Hello October | 1 October post, planner cover | 6–12 words | Hello October. Last quarter, first scarf. |
| Cosy and leaves | Story caption, letter board | 6–14 words | Lamps on at five, and nobody complaining. |
| Halloween countdown | Story or status, 24–31 October | 4–12 words | Pumpkins bought, carving date pending. |
| Motivational | Planner, work chat, journal | 4–11 words | You do not need January to start again. October will do. |

Short captions win on a phone screen. The verse is better on paper, where nobody scrolls past it.

## Ending October on the 31st with one Halloween page

October ends on Halloween, 31 October, every year. The [interactive Halloween card](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween) takes your letter, up to six photos and a word to carve on the pumpkin, and takes about five minutes to make. They knock three times on a little haunted house, carve a jack-o'-lantern until your word glows, and read your letter by flashlight in a dark attic: put the Keats or Frost line there.

It has partner, bestie, family and kids modes, and it ends with "Will you be my boo?" and a 1080×1920 Boo License marked "Valid every 31 October, forever". You get an email the first time they answer.

For a countdown, the [cinematic Halloween page](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween-premium) adds an optional unlock time: until then the link shows only their name and a countdown. It also takes a voice note of up to 60 seconds.

Start early: for Raksha Bandhan 2026, the nearest festival we have measured, 49.4% of pages were built on the day itself. That is a different festival and a small sample, n = 89.

## When an October quote is the wrong choice

Neither page is a party tool. Both are one-person greeting pages with an English interface, so for a group chat, a classroom or a shop window, post or print the quote instead.

October is not Halloween for everyone. In India it often carries Navratri, Dussehra or Diwali, and UK Bonfire Night follows on 5 November. And for a printed product sold in the UK, use Keats, Thoreau or Jackson rather than Frost.

- Thoreau, H. D. (1863). [Excursions](https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/9846), including "Autumnal Tints" (1862). Project Gutenberg.
- Jackson, H. H. (1886). [A Calendar of Sonnets](https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/9825). Project Gutenberg.
- Frost, R. (1913). [A Boy's Will](https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/3021). Project Gutenberg.
- SUNY College of Environmental Science and Forestry. [Why Leaves Change Color](https://www.esf.edu/ecenter/eis/leaves.php). Undated.

Results: success.com (x2), bookroo.com (4 book quotes, thin), goodgoodgood.co (85), trvst.world (48), s.gr-assets.com (Goodreads asset-host mirror), capcut.com (off-intent birthday page), blog.journey.cloud (SaaS blog list), katiegilley.com (personal blog, self-declared unverified attributions). 'october quotes' is a head term; long-tail alternatives: 'hello october quotes for instagram', 'public domain october poems with source', 'short october quotes for letter board'.

Brief claims checked: (a) Frost's 'October' is public domain only in the US — Frost died 1963, so it is in copyright in life+70 jurisdictions (UK/EU) until end-2033; the body says so. (b) Helen Hunt Jackson's 'October's Bright Blue Weather' and Emily Brontë's 'Fall, leaves, fall' are NOT on Project Gutenberg in any edition found (Gutenberg search for Jackson and Brontë; only the 1846 Bell Poems, which lacks it), so neither was quoted; Jackson's verified 'October' sonnet (A Calendar of Sonnets, 1886) replaces the first. (c) Keats 'To Autumn' is 1819 composition, 1820 publication — both stated. (d) Thoreau's 'Autumnal Tints' text is headed [1862.] in Excursions (1863).
